revision_notes: Variation 3 of 3 of the hook, built on v7 alone. Variations 1 and 2 (v8 and v9) are left as they were. Jonathan rated v7 7/10 and chose a sampled house piano for the hook. For this variation he asked for a new house piano vamp. It is a two-bar call and answer of off-beat chord stabs on steps 2, 5, 9, 11 and 13: the 'and' of one, the 'e' of two, the 'e' and the 'a' of three, and the 'e' of four. None of these meets the bass, the snare or any kick, so the hook still lives in the bass's gaps. The stabs are clipped to under half a step, and only the answer's last chord is held. A short top line rides on the stabs. The call plays B, D, then D moving to E, then D and B, and ends on B as a question. The answer plays B, D, E, then a short G (v7's peak note), and resolves on a held E. The top line never changes. Only the chords under it move with the E E C D cycle, so the hook is recognisable within its first two bars. Under each top note sit the two nearest tones of the pad's own chord, a little softer: E minor eleventh colours without the third over E, C major seventh and ninth over C, and D six-nine and sus shapes over D. No stab note is below B3, and the only G over E is the top line's own. A piano cannot slide, so the D-to-E slide becomes a chord move on step 9, off the snare: the D chord is struck lightly, and 50 ms later the E chord lands at full strength. Variations 1 and 2 measured hollow in the upper mids, and in v9 the listening model mistook the piano's low octave for the bass. So this piano sits high and bright, with no octave below anywhere. It uses the hardest sample layers, a very short damper, a 200 Hz high-pass, a 4 dB dip at 300 Hz, a 5 dB bite at 2.8 kHz and a 5 dB shelf above 4 kHz. Compression is firm and fast, the top is shaved, and there is a little chorus and room. The stabs stay centred. Section by section: in A, the stabs play with the top line doubled an octave up and widened. The space has only the grace dyad, once a bar, into the echo. Section B adds the top line two octaves up as sparkle, and a left-hand root and fifth at C4 or above on steps 2 and 9. The wall has the full stack, and the stabs gain a fourth voice from bar 41, where v7 added the fourths guitar. The stop is one ringing E chord with no third (E3, B3, E4, B4 and E5), rolled 5 ms a note. The coda has the top line alone, dry and mono, with the answer's E held into the tape stop, so the piece still ends on its hook. All hook guitars and the organ body are gone. As in v8 and v9, their notes are still generated and then dropped, so no timing or noise stream moves. The wall fuzz's old notes followed v7's contour and would clash with the vamp, so they leave too, and the fuzz now plays the new top line an octave up on its own seed. It stays at -17 dB, quietly under the piano, about 17 dB below the piano in the mid band, so it adds grit without masking the 2.8 kHz bite. The drums, swing, bass and its lock with the kick, form, tempo, bridge keys, pads and drone are exactly as in v7. Measured levels in the mid band against the mix: the stabs are at -2.5 dB in A, -3.3 dB in B and -3.4 dB in the wall. With their stacks, the group is at about -1.2, -1.7 and -1.9 dB. The octave-up stack is at -7 to -8 dB, the sparkle at about -14 dB and the left hand at -11 to -12 dB. The coda piano is at -0.1 dB, the echoed grace at -5.2 dB and the stop chord at -6.5 dB. The bass is at -3.4 dB, the kick at -8.3 dB and the drone at -15.5 dB, within 0.2 dB of their v7 levels. The 1-4 kHz share is 14.0 per cent, up from 8.1 in v9. The low mids are down from 32.4 to 21.8 per cent, and the spectral centroid is up from 611 to 695 Hz. Presence (4-10 kHz) moved only from 2.2 to 2.5 per cent, short of the 3.5 per cent aimed for, because the piano recordings carry little energy there. Four drafts set the balance. In the first, the octave stacks measured 7 and 14 dB under the stabs, so they were raised. The second drew the kick 0.3 dB down against the mix, so the piano's weight moved up into the bite and shelf, and the stabs came down 1 dB. The limiter's peak reduction is 5.1 dB, against 5.0 in v9 and 4.5 in v7. Its peaks are the untouched drum and bass transients. Softening the stabs beside the kicks was tried in a fourth draft, but it raised the master gain and the limiter to 5.2 dB, so it was reverted.
